topStories.headline: Four Clarion Alley Murals Wiped Out After Property Owner Orders 'Graffiti' Cleanup
topStories.dek: A building manager painted over four works in the iconic Mission District alleyway last week, leaving the 34-year-old mural collective scrambling to assess the damage and seek city support.
topStories.body:
Four murals in Clarion Alley, the iconic Mission District passage with over 50 murals connecting Mission and Valencia streets, were painted over last week — three completely, one partially. The incident happened on a Monday when a neighbor saw a man painting over the works; by the time artist Doug Rhodes, who has a studio on the alley, spotted him, the worker was already on his fourth mural.

A representative from the Clarion Alley Mural Project said the organization reached out to Makras Real Estate, the company that manages the building, and received an email stating that the property owner had ordered an employee to paint over what was reported as "graffiti." The Clarion Alley Mural Project said in a statement that it "has had both written and verbal agreements and understandings with property owners and landlords regarding murals on Clarion Alley for 34, going on 35 years." A CAMP representative said the murals can be restored, though the cost remains unclear.

The loss drew an immediate response from the District 9 supervisor's office. "The destruction of these iconic murals is devastating and we hope that it was an inadvertent mistake that can be remedied quickly," said Jennifer Ferrigno, a legislative aide to Supervisor Jackie Fielder. "Our office is ready to support our community partners to restore the artwork and care for this historic alley." Fielder's office met with CAMP representatives last week to explore ways the city can support the organization.

topStories.headline: Bernal Heights House Fire Injures Three Firefighters, Displaces Family of Seven
topStories.dek: A two-alarm blaze gutted the first floor of a home on Anderson Street on Wednesday morning, sending smoke over the neighborhood and narrowly sparing two adjacent houses.
topStories.body:
A morning fire at a home in San Francisco's Bernal Heights neighborhood sent smoke billowing over the area, injured three firefighters, and displaced a family of seven. A cat also died in the blaze. San Francisco fire crews responded to the 700 block of Anderson Street at about 6:30 a.m. on Wednesday, September 2, and contained the fire by 7:23 a.m.

Arriving firefighters found the first floor of the home engulfed. A second alarm was called due to "exposures being threatened," according to SFist, and two homes directly on either side of the burning structure were apparently saved from damage. One family member, Giselle Basilio, described a smoke-filled escape through the hallway before reaching the front door safely.

The San Francisco Fire Department did not immediately release information on the cause of the fire or the extent of the three firefighters' injuries. The displaced family of seven was assisted by the Red Cross.

topStories.headline: Bernal Heights Blackout Is San Francisco's Seventh Major PG&E Outage of 2026
topStories.dek: An unplanned outage cut power to roughly 2,825 customers in Bernal Heights on August 29, the latest in a pattern of failures keeping pressure on the utility's grid maintenance.
topStories.body:
Power was restored to more than 8,800 Pacific Gas and Electric customers in San Francisco after a pair of unplanned outages on Saturday, August 29. About 2,825 customers in the Bernal Heights area lost power starting at 5:04 p.m. and regained it by 6 p.m., according to a PG&E spokesperson. Hoodline identified the event as San Francisco's seventh major blackout of 2026.

The San Francisco Department of Emergency Management confirmed the outage and reminded residents that they can sign up for localized alerts through its AlertSF system by texting their ZIP code to 888-777. The frequency of 2026's outages has kept scrutiny on PG&E's grid maintenance practices, a pattern that dates at least to a December 2025 fire.

The Mission District and Bernal Heights have been hit repeatedly this year. In June, 1,600 customers in the Mission District and Castro experienced a separate hour-long blackout around 4 a.m., and more than 600 customers near 22nd and 24th streets lost power on a Thursday evening the same week. PG&E said the cause of the August 29 Bernal Heights outage was under investigation.

moreNews.headline: Portal Cinema Kickstarter Deadline September 18 as October Opening Approaches
moreNews.body:
As reported last week, The Portal Cinema is set to open at 3293 Mission St., near 29th Street, sometime in October, according to the cinema's website — an update Mission Local confirmed on September 3. The nonprofit, 45-seat single-screen venue will offer more than 11 screenings a week spanning repertory, new releases, global contemporary cinema, and artists' moving-image work, with DCP, 35mm, and 16mm projection formats.

Founder Nellie Killian's $250,000 Kickstarter campaign closes September 18. According to SFist, $50,000 is still needed to complete a PG&E panel upgrade required for 35mm projection and to run a new HVAC system. Organizational supporters can contact Killian directly through the cinema's website.

moreNews.headline: Bodycam Footage Contradicts SFPD Account of Pride Weekend Stud Alley Arrests
moreNews.body: Internal police documents and body camera footage reviewed by Mission Local show that San Francisco police officers did not issue dispersal orders immediately before arresting 18 people at the "Stud Alley" party on Washburn Street on June 27, 2026. The records show a lieutenant told investigators he "did not give a dispersal order prior to the skirmish line moving," and that he feared doing so would prevent officers from seizing the party's sound equipment. The investigation, published September 2, adds new detail to a Pride weekend enforcement action that District 9 Supervisor Jackie Fielder had already flagged in a June 30 letter to the mayor and police chief.
